prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a downward-angled egocentric view of the seated camera wearer's lower body and outstretched arms in the bottom foreground (0.2 to 0.6 m away), a standing child in a white shirt directly in front and to the upper-left (0.3 to 1.2 m away), and a raised mud platform with three round pots and lids on the ground to the right (roughly 1.0 to 1.5 m away, spaced 0.2 to 0.3 m apart). In frames 1 to 4, the child stands facing away and slightly right while within arm's reach of both the camera wearer's hands and the nearest pot, with the child's head cropped out of the top of the frame and a blurry foreground object at less than 0.2 m occluding the lower-left of frame 1. Across the five frames, the child's upper torso shifts from very bright (0.3 to 0.5 m) in frames 1 to 4 to noticeably darker (0.8 to 1.2 m) in frame 5 as the child steps forward and away toward a vertical wooden post on the upper-right, pulling out of the wearer's reach. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering of the child's overhanging shirt, the linked hands below it, and the wearer's lap beneath, while also revealing the 3D rim concavity of the ground pots despite harsh sunlight and shadows. However, the depth map is unreliable along the stepped ledge of the mud platform where the height drop is smoothed out, and in frame 5 where the wearer's lower-left knee appears overly bright compared to the adjacent arms.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map outlines the standing child in the upper-left/center (0.3 to 1.2 m from the camera wearer) and the seated camera wearer's lower body and arms in the bottom half (0.2 to 0.6 m away), while leaving the ground, mud ledge,wooden post, and pots at 1.0 to 1.5 m unsegmented in black. In frames 1 to 4, the child and the camera wearer are at 0 m separation where their hands touch in the center foreground within the wearer's arm's reach, before separating by about 0.5 m in frame 5 as the child walks away with their back turned and head out of view above the frame. When separate masks appear in frames 2, 4, and 5, they help distinguish the child's overhanging torso and right arm above from the camera wearer's arms and lap below, which partially occlude the child's lower legs. However, the map is highly unreliable: it merges the wearer and child into a single 'person' mask in frames 1 and 3, splits the child's own body into two separate 'person' instances in frame 5, and completely misses the wearer's body in frame 5. It also hallucinates false object classes, mislabeling the wearer's left forearm as a 'cup' in frame 2 and the sunlit row of three pots and lids on the right ground as 'scissors' in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely black and fails to detect any yellow body skeletons for either the seated camera wearer (0.2 to 0.6 m away) or the standing child (0.3 to 1.2 m away), and misses all hands in frames 1, 2, and 5. In frame 3, a single magenta hand skeleton localizes the camera wearer's right hand at roughly 0.4 m distance in the center foreground, angled upward and to the left where it clasps the child's right hand within arm's reach below the child's torso. In frame 4, a single magenta hand skeleton shifts to the camera wearer's left hand at roughly 0.4 m distance in the lower-center foreground, oriented upward and to the right as it holds the child's fingers just before the child steps away in frame 5. These two skeletons isolate the exact 3D finger articulation and palm orientation of the wearer's active hands amid the overlapping limbs and patterned clothing in the RGB frames. Overall, the pose map is largely unreliable because extreme top-down foreshortening, cropping of the child's head and shoulders at the top edge, and mutual hand occlusion cause total detection failure across most of the sequence.
